2298425.title: Third Meeting of Hindi Advisory Committee of Ministry of Ayush Held in New Delhi
2298425.body_html:
AYUSH
Third Meeting of Hindi Advisory Committee of Ministry of Ayush Held in New Delhi
Hindi Plays an Important Role in Strengthening Good Governance and Taking Ayush to the People: Shri Prataprao Jadhav
Emphasis on Strengthening Use of Hindi and Public Outreach in Ministry of Ayush
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi

The third meeting of the Hindi Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Ayush was held today at Kartavya Bhawan-I, New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

The meeting was attended by Hon’ble Members of Parliament Shri Rahul Singh Lodhi and Shri Gyaneshwar Patil, along with Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, members of the Committee and senior officials of the Ministry and its subordinate institutions.

Addressing the meeting, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that the Hindi Advisory Committee is not merely a formal body but an important platform for strengthening the use and promotion of Hindi in the Ministry and making it an effective medium for public welfare and communication.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav said that the country is moving forward with the vision of ‘Viksit Bharat @2047’. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has laid special emphasis on the preservation, promotion and wider use of Indian languages. Shri Jadhav noted that the Prime Minister’s consistent use of Hindi at national and international forums has enhanced the recognition and respect for Hindi globally.

Shri Jadhav said that he makes efforts to ensure that maximum official work in his office is undertaken in Hindi. He urged officers and employees not to view the use of Hindi merely as a formal or constitutional obligation, but to make it an effective instrument of good governance, transparency and public outreach and an integral part of their day-to-day work.

Highlighting the importance of Indian languages in the Ayush sector, Shri Jadhav said that Ayush represents India’s rich and ancient knowledge tradition. Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy are gaining increasing popularity not only in India but also across the world.

Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, highlighted the efforts being made by the Ministry to promote the use of Hindi in official work, correspondence, publications, website, social media and public relations activities. He also informed the Committee about initiatives to encourage officers and employees to use Hindi through training programmes, workshops and incentive schemes.

The Committee discussed the need to make Ayush-related knowledge, research, scientific literature, public welfare schemes and achievements of the Ministry widely available in Hindi and other Indian languages. The members also deliberated on making Ayush-related information more accessible through Indian languages and further strengthening its outreach among the general public.

The Ministry’s Hindi house journal ‘Apratim Ayush’ was also released during the meeting. Smt. Purnima Bose, Deputy Director, Department of Official Language, Ministry of Ayush, welcomed the participants, while Dr. Prakash Kumar, Assistant Director, Ministry of Ayush, conducted the proceedings.

The meeting was also attended by non-official members Markandey Rai, Thinles Dorje, Sunil Mehru, Ramya Krishna Kanaparthi and Hemchandra Vaidya.

2298395.title: BHARAT TAXI ROLL OUT
2298395.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
BHARAT TAXI ROLL OUT
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi

Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led digital App mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society is officially launched in the cities of Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.

The implementation of Bharat Taxi Services is being carried out in a phased manner across the country. The implementation includes registration and onboarding of Sarathis (drivers), customer enrolment, training programmes and expansion of services to identified cities and States. As on 04.08.2026, the platform has registered 8.48 lakh Sarathis (drivers) and 44.27 lakh customers. The platform is facilitating 11,106 daily rides and has enabled cumulative earnings of ₹83.70 crore for Sarathis.

The rollout of services of Bharat Taxi, operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), in other cities and States is subject to operational requirements and necessary approvals. Expansion is undertaken based on factors such as operational preparedness, availability of Sarathis, completion of statutory requirements, and coordination with the concerned State Governments, cooperative institutions, and other stakeholders.

The details of operation of Bharat Taxi in various cities and average daily rides, as on 04.08.2026, are as under:

Bharat Taxi and Yatri Sathi are separate mobility platforms operating under different institutional frameworks. Bharat Taxi is a cooperative-based mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002, whereas Yatri Sathi is a mobility platform developed and operated by the Department of Information Technology and Electronics (DITE), Government of West Bengal.

On 19th July, 2026, STCL entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Government of West Bengal for collaboration with the Yatri Sathi platform. Under the MoU, Bharat Taxi extends support in the areas of driver enrolment, cooperative membership, driver welfare and public outreach.

 

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

2298389.title: NEW COURSES AT TRIBHUVAN COOPERATIVE UNIVERSITY (TSU)
2298389.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
NEW COURSES AT TRIBHUVAN COOPERATIVE UNIVERSITY (TSU)
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi

The University launched three new MBA programmes during the academic year 2025–26:

  1. MBA in Cooperative Management
  2. MBA in Cooperative Banking and Finance
  3. MBA in Agribusiness Management

The University has also designed five certificate courses for the professional management of cooperative societies. The names of these certificate courses are as follows:

  1. Certificate Course in Business Management and Governance for the Secretaries and Staff of PACS (Primary Agricultural Credit Society)
  2. Certificate Course in Business Management and Governance for Secretaries and Staff of Primary Fisheries Cooperatives
  3. Certificate Course in Business Management and Governance for the Secretaries and Staff of Dairy Cooperative Societies
  4. Certificate Course in Leadership Development for the Board of Directors (BODs) of District Credit Cooperative Banks (DCCBs)
  5. Certificate Course in Cybersecurity for Cooperative Banks

The courses align with the need of PACS, Fisheries Cooperatives, Dairy Cooperatives and DCCBs.

While the new MBA programmes have been launched in 2025–26, the certificate courses are scheduled during 2026–27.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

2298385.title: AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL
2298385.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Cooperation has set up Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 to act as an apex organization for production, procurement, processing, branding, labelling, packaging, storage, marketing, distribution and strategic research & development of quality seeds with a clear vision to build a strong, farmer-centric seed system through a cooperative-led structure.

Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) has so far introduced seeds of 18 crops and 124 varieties in the market under the 'Bharat Beej' brand for distribution across the country. Further, BBSSL has undertaken initiatives for developing production and quality-testing requirements for vegetable seeds in accordance with the prescribed seed quality and regulatory standards.

During the financial year 2025–26, BBSSL produced 75,535 metric tonnes of seeds through its associated seed-producing farmers under the seed production programme for the 'Bharat Beej' brand. The programme facilitates farmers' participation in organised seed production and provides technical support for the production of seeds in accordance with the prescribed quality and certification standards.

For the conservation of traditional indigenous varieties, BBSSL has initiated a programme in Uttarakhand focusing on the identification, conservation, multiplication and documentation of such varieties. BBSSL's activities include the expansion of domestic seed production, conservation of indigenous genetic resources, and distribution of quality seeds through the cooperative network, thereby contributing to the objective of reducing the country's dependence on imported seeds and strengthening self-reliance in the seed sector.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

2298390.title: Affordable and Accessible Healthcare for All
2298390.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Affordable and Accessible Healthcare for All
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi

In past 12 years, the Government of India has significantly strengthened India’s health system. Quality healthcare is more accessible, more affordable, and more equitable than it has ever been.  This aligns with the principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas” to build an Atmanirbhar Bharat.

Ayushman Bharat

  • The Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) provides health insurance of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year to families from the poorest 40% of society and all senior citizens aged 70 and above.  

    • Over 40,000 claims are processed every single day for over 1,900 treatment packages.

    • Since the scheme launched in 2018, as of August 12, 2026:

      • Over 45.5 crore Ayushman Cards have been issued

      • 12.69 crore hospitalizations have been covered, amounting to Rs. 1.92 lakh crore (as on June 30, 2026)

      • Over 38,466 public and private hospitals are empanelled

      • 1.20 crore senior citizens enrolled under the Ayushman Bharat Vay Vandana scheme. Over 13.84 lakh treatments, worth Rs. 3,000-crore have been availed.

      • Under AB PM-JAY, 29.05 lakh inter-state portability hospital admissions, amounting to more than Rs. 8,383.97 crore, have been authorised (as on June 30, 2026)

  • Over 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) are now functional across the country to provide primary healthcare at every neighbourhood (As of 12 August 2026). These centres offer 12 free services and have recorded a cumulative footfall of over 540 crore till date.

  • The Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM):

    • Support for 23,224 rural health and wellness centres in 10 high-focus states.

    • Establishing 13,736 urban health and wellness centres in all states.

    • 3,389 block public health units in 11 high-focus states.

    • Setting up 744 integrated public health labs in all districts.

    • Establishing 631 critical care hospital blocks in all districts with a population of more than 5 lakh.

  • And underpinning all of this is India’s digital health backbone, the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). Coverage under ABDM (as of August 12, 2026):

    • 96.43 crore ABHA health identity numbers created

    • Over 110 crore health records have been linked with ABHA

    • Over 5.47 lakh health facilities have been registered on the platform

    • More than 10.50 lakh healthcare professionals have been registered on the platform.

 

National Health Mission: Targeted Health Interventions

The National Health Mission (NHM), with its two sub-missions-National Rural Health Mission and National Urban Health Mission, delivers targeted programmes that address specific diseases, populations, and health challenges. NHM has significantly improved public health outcomes across maternal and child health, disease elimination, and immunisation.

Maternal and Child Health: Making Safe Births the Norm

 

  • The Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan has enabled over 7.91 crore free antenatal check-ups.

    • More than 1.24 crore high-risk pregnancies have been identified.

    • First-trimester antenatal registration in India increased from 58.6% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 76.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).

    • Mothers receiving four or more antenatal care visits in India increased significantly from 51.2% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 65.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).

    • Institutional deliveries in India increased from 78.9% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 90.6% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).

  • On immunisation, the Universal Immunisation Programme reaches 2.67 crore newborns and 2.9 crore pregnant women every year with free vaccines against 12 diseases.

  • Mission Indradhanush, launched in 2014, has functioned as a catch-up drive, vaccinating 5.46 crore children and 1.32 crore pregnant women across its various phases.

  • The percentage of zero-dose children-those who had received no vaccines at all-dropped from 0.11% of the population in 2023 to 0.06% in 2024.

  • Under Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP), the government launched U-WIN in October 2024 — a platform that ensures no family loses its vaccination records. As of March 2026, 11.87 crore children and 3.96 crore pregnant women are already registered.

  • In February 2026, the government launched a three-month campaign to provide free HPV vaccines to 1.2 crore girls aged 14 years, for combating cervical cancer.

    • 52,10,302 girls have received the HPV vaccine across the country (as on July 15, 2026).

  • These initiatives have improved various mortality rates, including:

    • Maternal mortality rate declined to 87 per 1,00,000 live births in 2022-24 from 130 per 1,00,000 in 2014-16.

    • Neonatal mortality rate declined to 17 per 1,000 live births in 2023 from 28 per 1,000 live births in 2015.

    • Under-5 mortality rate declined to 28 per 1,000 live births in 2023 from 48 per 1,000 live births in 2015.

Eliminating Communicable Diseases: Real Progress on Long-Standing Burdens

  • The government has reduced the prevalence of communicable diseases over the past 12 years.

  • New cases of tuberculosis emerging yearly in India dipped by 21% from 2015-2024; mortality due to TB dropped by 28% during the same period.

    • Treatment success rates in Tuberculosis have climbed from 83% in 2021 to 90% in 2025 — and treatment coverage has gone from 53% (2015) to 92% (2024).

    • More than 28.1 crore people have already been screened, 20 Lakh people given preventive treatment, and 5.7 lakh new Nikshay Mitras have been added so far under the intensified campaigns since December 2024.

  • Malaria cases and deaths have fallen by 80.5% and 78.38% respectively between 2015 and 2023. India exited the WHO's 'High Burden to High Impact (HBHI) group' for malaria in 2024.

Non-Communicable Diseases: Catching Problems Early

  • National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD) focuses on strengthening infrastructure, human resource development, screening, early diagnosis, referral, treatment, and health promotion for Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs). Through nationwide screening drives:

    • 41.5 crore Screened for hypertension

    • 41.3 crore for diabetes

    • 35.3 crore for oral cancer and

    • 16.5 crore for breast cancer.

  • The Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (launched 2016) has provided free dialysis to 32.44 lakh patients across 1,856 centres (as of June, 2026).

  • Under the Strengthening of Tertiary Cancer Care Centres Facilities Scheme, 19 State Cancer Institutes (SCIs) and 20 Tertiary Cancer Care Centers (TCCCs) have been approved.

  • Under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases, 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres (DCCCs) and 6,410 NCD clinics at Community Health Centres have been set up across the country.

  • India has achieved a 17.3% relative reduction in overall tobacco use from 2009-10 to 2016-17, as per the Report of the second round of the Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS- 2).

    • To achieve a tobacco-free generation, the Government launched the Tobacco Free Youth Campaign in 2023 — now in its third edition. This work has earned India the 2025 Bloomberg Philanthropies Award for tobacco control.

 

Making Medicines and Tests Actually Affordable

 

  • The Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) has made generic medicines cheaper. The Jan Aushadhi Kendras, where these medicines are available, have grown from a handful of stores in 2014-15 to over 18,646 Jan Aushadhi Kendras as of February 2026.

  • These medicines are sold at 50–80% below branded prices, with a basket of over 2,000 medicines and 300 surgical devices.

  • AMRIT (Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment) Pharmacies launched in 2015, go even further, offering life-saving medicines at discounts of 50–90%, making treatment affordable for low-income patients who would otherwise go without treatment.

    • The scheme has benefited more than 6.85 crore patients and medicines worth over Rs. 17,000 crore at MRP have been dispensed so far, resulting in cumulative savings of about Rs. 8,400 crore for patients.

  • Free Diagnostics Service Initiative under NHM makes tests, X-rays, blood work free at every level of the public health system from sub-centres all the way up to district hospitals, spanning haematology, radiology, biochemistry, and more.

    • Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities

      • 14 tests at Sub Centers

      • 63 at Primary Health Centers

      • 97 at Community Health Centres

      • 111 tests at Sub District Hospitals

      • 134 tests at District Hospitals.

Reaching People Where They Are: Digital Health and Telemedicine

  • eSanjeevani, India's national telemedicine platform, has delivered over 49 crore consultations since its launch in 2019 (as on August 11, 2026). Over 2.4 lakh healthcare providers are now on the platform.

  • Tele-MANAS — launched in October 2022 — was introduced as a toll-free helpline (14416) available nationwide, offering a wide range of mental health services. 

  • It operates in 20 languages across all 36 states and union territories. It has already received 43.64 lakh calls since the launch of the service, through 53 Tele-Manas Cells and 23 Mentoring Institutes (as on August 11, 2026).

  • i-DRONE service launched in 2021 is delivering medicines and vaccines by drone. 22,000 medicines have been delivered over 7,700 kilometres through 65 healthcare centres.

  • AI is now also embedded in care delivery. Between April 2023 and November 2025, 28.2 crore eSanjeevani consultations were supported by AI-enabled Clinical Decision Support Systems, providing real-time clinical alerts to doctors.

Building the Workforce India Needs

  • Over the past 12 years, the number of medical colleges has more than doubled — from 387 to 818 allopathy colleges (as of 2025-2026).

  • 12 new AIIMS have been made functional since 2014. There are 23 AIIMS now.

  • MBBS and PG seats increased to 1,28,976 and 85,822, respectively, as of 2025-26.

  • Nursing has received equal attention. 157 new nursing colleges are being set up, adding around 15,700 nursing graduates annually.

    • B.Sc. Nursing seats are up 53% to 1,27,290, and M.Sc. Nursing seats up 39% to 14,986 as of June 2025.

Alternative Healthcare

Alongside modern medicine, the government has formally integrated traditional healthcare systems into the public health framework. The Ministry of AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa Rigpa, and Homeopathy), formed in November 2014, has established traditional medicines as an active part of India's health system.

  • 942 AYUSH institutions exist in the country as of May 2025.

  • Ayush Grid is India’s digital bridge between traditional healing and modern healthcare delivery, making AYUSH more accessible, integrated, and future-ready. This AYUSH Grid will digitally connect all AYUSH hospitals and laboratories nationwide.

2298378.title: OBJECTIVE OF THE RANKING FRAMEWORK FOR COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES
2298378.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
OBJECTIVE OF THE RANKING FRAMEWORK FOR COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:10PM by PIB Delhi

Using the National Cooperative Database (NCD), a ranking framework has been introduced to rank the primary cooperative societies, sector wise and State / district / block wise. The Ranking Framework was launched on 24.01.2025. It enables the Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS) of State / UT to generate rankings of primary cooperative societies of 12 sectors through the NCD portal. This Ranking Framework helps to enhance transparency, efficiency, and effectiveness within the societies, while also improving their credibility and competitive capability.

 

The ranking framework enables State/ UT RCS to assess the performance of cooperative societies based on five broad categories / parameters, namely audit compliance, operational activities, financial performance, infrastructure, and basic identity information. Under the Ranking Framework, weightage scores have generally been assigned to these categories in the aforesaid order, with an overall weightage of 100 marks.

 

The Cooperative Ranking Framework is an important step towards strengthening the cooperative sector, providing cooperatives with actionable insights, benchmarks for performance, and an opportunity to foster competition and innovation. This ranking framework can be used for dissemination of best practices of the top-performing cooperative societies in each sector, so that other societies can learn and adopt these best practices.

 

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

2298375.title: BENCHMARKS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS OF NCOL
2298375.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
BENCHMARKS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS OF NCOL
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:09PM by PIB Delhi

National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) markets its certified organic products under the "Bharat Organics" brand through a multi-channel marketing strategy. Its products are marketed via various e-commerce platforms, modern retail chains, cooperative outlets including Safal/Mother Dairy, NAFED, NCCF, etc., and its Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) portal.

The benchmark for organic production in India is the National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP), which is notified by the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA). National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) complies with these benchmarks by procuring and marketing only certified organic products that conform to NPOP standards. The products are sourced from valid certified farmer groups, Internal Control Systems (ICS), or certified operators and are subject to stringent quality testing, traceability mechanisms, and compliance with applicable food safety and organic certification requirements. In addition, NCOL ensures mandatory laboratory testing of organic produce for pesticide residues and other quality parameters before marketing, thereby maintaining the prescribed standards for organic production in India.

NCOL promotes the formation of National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP)-certified Internal Control System (ICS) groups through cooperative societies to support organic farmers. It facilitates the procurement of certified organic produce through cooperative societies at fair and transparent prices and markets organic products under the Bharat Organics brand through multiple sales channels. NCOL has signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with 28 States/UTs to promote the organic cooperative ecosystem and facilitate greater participation of farmers in organic farming.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

2298371.title: BHARAT TAXI - COOPERATIVE-MODEL MOBILITY PLATFORM
2298371.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
BHARAT TAXI - COOPERATIVE-MODEL MOBILITY PLATFORM
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:07PM by PIB Delhi

Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led digital App mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society is officially launched in the cities of Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan. As on 04.08.2026, the platform has 8.48 lakh registered Sarathis (drivers) and 44.27 lakh registered customers.

The rollout of services of Bharat Taxi in other cities and States is taken by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) subject to operational requirements and necessary approvals. Expansion is undertaken based on factors such as operational preparedness, availability of Sarathis, completion of statutory requirements, and coordination with the concerned State Governments, cooperative institutions, and other stakeholders.

Bharat Taxi has adopted a cooperative-led operating framework to ensure affordability, transparency, and driver welfare. Key measures include:

  1.  Adoption of a zero-commission model for drivers;
  2.  Transparent and predictable fare structures without hidden charges;
  3.  Subscription-based participation to stabilise driver earnings
  4.  Facilitation of social security measures such as insurance coverage and welfare linkages for driver-members; and
  5. Expansion through collaboration with State Governments, cooperative institutions, and public bodies to enhance adoption and accessibility.

Bharat Taxi, run by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) is registered under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002. The Society functions in accordance with the provisions of the Act and its registered Bye-laws. No financial support has been provided by the Government for expansion of  Bharat Taxi platform.

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

2298369.title: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY IN THE COOPERATIVE SECTOR
2298369.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY IN THE COOPERATIVE SECTOR
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Cooperation has undertaken several reformative measures during the last three years to promote digital technology, transparency and good governance in the cooperative sector under the vision of "Sahkar Se Samriddhi". The major initiatives and their outcomes are as under:-

  1. Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) Project: The Ministry is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of functional PACS with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 Crore which has now been increased up to 2925.39 Crore which entails bringing all the functional PACS onto an ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based common national software, linking them with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs). This has been done with a view to improving their operational efficiency, transparency and accountability through ERP-based National Software. The project facilitates standardized accounting, audit, MIS, online service delivery and integration with various national digital platforms, thereby enabling efficient governance and better service delivery to members. Under the Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) Project, 63,686 PACS have been onboarded on the ERP-based National Software, 54,707 PACS have been declared as e-PACS and more than 51.58 crore digital transactions have been carried out through the software as on 15.07.2026, leading to enhanced transparency, improved service delivery and better financial management at the grassroots level.

    To promote digital technology and transparency, the ePACS software includes the following features:

  1. Comprehensive functional coverage: The software comprises 22 ERP modules covering the entire spectrum of PACS operations, including credit (loan origination, sanction, disbursement and recovery), deposits, accounting, audit, member management, procurement and other business functions of PACS.
  2. Standardised, CAS-MIS compliant accounting: The software generates books of accounts and financial statements in conformity with the Common Accounting System and Management Information System (CAS-MIS) norms, thereby bringing uniformity in accounting practices across PACS in the country.
  3. Interoperability and integration: The software supports integration with Aadhaar-enabled services, Core Banking Systems (CBS) of StCBs/DCCBs, Point of Sale (PoS) devices, Common Service Centres (CSC), the National Cooperative Database (NCD) and State-specific portals, enabling PACS to function as part of a larger digital ecosystem.
  4. Digital credit delivery: The software provides facilities such as end-to-end loan origination, KCC processing and mobile application support, facilitating faster and more transparent credit delivery to members.
  5. Secure cloud architecture: Data of all onboarded PACS is maintained on secure, centralised cloud-based storage with appropriate cyber security safeguards, dispensing with dependence on standalone local systems and physical records.
  6. Internal controls and on-system audit: The software incorporates maker-checker functionality and an on-system audit module, enabling continuous monitoring of transactions and conduct of statutory audit directly on the system.
  7. Dashboards, analytics and MIS: Dashboards, analytics and MIS reports are available to higher-tier stakeholders for monitoring and decision support.
  8. Multi-lingual capability: A key feature of the software is its multi-lingual capability, which enables PACS personnel to operate the software in regional languages. At present, the software is available in 20 languages.
  9. State-specific customisation: While the core software is common across the country, it is customisable to accommodate State-specific bye-laws, products, processes and reporting requirements.
  10. Till date, loan details of 4.02 crore borrowers of PACS, amounting to ₹2.3 lakh crore, have been digitised and are available to authorised stakeholders on ePACS.
  11. Deposit details of 5.49 crore depositors, amounting to about ₹37,000 crore, have also been digitised.
  12. Membership records of 10.30 crore members are now available on ePACS. These PACS-wise, member-wise records, which were hitherto available only through physical access, are now on ePACS.
  13. The CSC portal has been integrated with ePACS, enabling PACS to function as Common Service Centres and offer citizen-centric services. Integration with PMKSK, AgriStack and PMBJK are at advanced stages.
  14. NABARD is in the process of implementing end-to-end digitisation of the loan process through ePACS, followed by integration with the Krishi Rin Portal (KRP), to ensure efficient loan sanction and disbursement as well as targeted delivery of interest subvention benefits to members.
  15. Through integration with the AgriStack portal, the farmer profile, land and crop details of farmers, as well as Scale of Finance (SoF) details, can be utilised for processing and sanctioning loans in the ePACS system. Further, the details of loans sanctioned through ePACS will be shared with KRP using Aadhaar as the common identifier, ensuring that interest subvention benefits are directed to loanees on an Aadhaar-authenticated basis.
  16. A phased implementation strategy is also followed for integrating ePACS with the Core Banking Solutions (CBS) of DCCBs to enable both seven-day loan disbursal and the “paperless to cashless” goal. As this integration entails work at both the ePACS and the CBS levels, the CBS vendors of DCCBs are also required to participate in the process. The initial focus is on the TCS vendor, which covers 168 banks (StCBs/DCCBs) across 16 States, and the integration will subsequently be extended to other CBS vendors.
  17. Maker-checker controls: The software provides maker-checker functionality, whereby transactions are subjected to multiple levels of verification before authorisation, thereby strengthening internal controls and reducing operational risks.

 

  1. Computerisation of the Office of Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS): Centrally sponsored project for computerization of RCS offices in States/Union Territories has been launched by the Ministry on 30.01.2024 with a budgetary outlay of Rs.94.59 crore for three years w.e.f. 2023-24. This is a part of the umbrella project of “Strengthening Cooperatives Through IT Interventions” of the Ministry. The project aims to enhance the ease of doing business for Cooperative Societies and create a digital ecosystem for transparent, paperless interaction of cooperative societies with the RCS offices in all States/Union Territories. Under the project, grants are being provided to the States/ UTs for procurement of hardware, development of software, maintenance & upgradation of software, etc. The software developed under this scheme will be as per the Cooperative Acts of the respective States/UTs. During the financial years 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27 (up to 15th July, 2026), 35 States/UTs have submitted their proposals, and Rs 43.21 crore has been released as the Government of India's share to States/UTs. The integrated digital RCS portals of 7 States/UTs have been gone live and integrated with National Cooperative Database also.
  2. Computerization of Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (ARDBs): To strengthen the long-term cooperative credit structure, the project of computerization of 1,851 units of Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (ARDBs) spread across 13 States/ Union Territories has been approved by the Government. NABARD is the implementing agency for the project. So far, proposals from 10 States/UTs have been received and sanctioned with 1,422 units. Further, GOI share amounting to Rs 16.74 crore has been released to 10 States/UTs in FY 2023-24, FY 24-25, FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27 for procurement of hardware, digitization, and setting up of support systems. Till date, 9 States/UTs have procured the Hardware under the project.
  3. National Cooperative Database (NCD): A comprehensive database of cooperatives in the country has been developed with the support of State Governments to facilitate stakeholders in policy making and implementation of programmes/ schemes related to cooperatives across the country. The NCD portal was launched by Hon’ble Home & Cooperation Minister on 08.03.2024. So far, the database includes data on around 8.6 lakh cooperatives from 30 different sectors, involving approximately 32 crore members.
  4. Launch of National Cooperative Database (NCD) portal 3.0: The upgraded / enhanced version NCD portal 3.0 was officially launched by Hon'ble Home & Cooperation Minister on 06.07.2026. The NCD portal 3.0 provides several new features, including OTP-based secure login, cooperative society-level user access and dashboards, AI Chatbot, village-level GIS mapping, multilingual support through Bhashini integration, API integration with State RCS portals for real time updation of data, feedback mechanism, and call management and technical helpdesk support, improved frontend framework and database for enhanced security and faster access etc.
  5. Launch of NCD GeoTag Mobile Application: The NCD GeoTag Mobile Application has been developed for capturing the GPS location (latitude and longitude) of all functional cooperatives. It was launched on 06.07.2026 by Hon'ble Home & Cooperation Minister. The mobile application will also enable accurate geo-tagging and GIS-based mapping of cooperatives on the NCD Portal.
  6. Computerisation of the Office of Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS): The Office of Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies has been computerized to create a digital ecosystem for Multi-State Cooperative Societies by enabling online registration, amendment of bye-laws and time-bound delivery of services.
  7. Cooperative Ranking Framework: The Government launched the Cooperative Ranking Framework on 24th January 2025 to assess and rank cooperatives, State-wise and sector-wise. This ranking framework enables State RCS to assess Cooperative Societies’ performance based on key parameters, including audit compliance, operational activities, financial performance, infrastructure, and basic identity information. The States/ UTs can generate rankings of Cooperative Societies of 12 major sectors, namely PACS, Dairy, Fishery, Urban Cooperative Banks, Housing, Credit and Thrift, and Khadi and Gram Udyog, Agro processing / Industrial, Handicraft, Handloom, Textile & Weavers, Multipurpose and Sugar at State, district, and block levels, through the NCD portal. This ranking system aims to enhance transparency, reliability and competitiveness among cooperative societies, ultimately fostering their growth.
  8. Facility for States / UTs to integrate State RCS portal with NCD portal through API: The Ministry of Cooperation (MoC) developed a standard API for States to fetch the entire data of cooperative societies of the State from the NCD portal to their respective RCS portals, and shared the Standard API Specification Document and database schema with States on 27.05.2025. Subsequently, the Ministry shared a document on Push APIs (End Point APIs) for live, event-driven data pushing from RCS portals to the NCD Portal, enabling real-time updates and new registration data, on 22.09.2025. To further clarify the process, an advisory along with a comprehensive checklist was issued to all States / UTs on 14.11.2025. As per the integration plan, States/UTs need to ensure the development of reverse/pull API at their end and complete RCS computerization in accordance with the checklist for successful integration with the NCD portal. As of 15.07.2026, the States of Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Mizoram and Sikkim, and UTs of Dadra and Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu and Andaman and Nicobar Islands have completed integration with the NCD portal. This two-way integration will ensure synchronization of cooperative data across platforms.
  9. Digital Services and Technology Integration: The ERP-based software developed for PACS supports integration with various digital platforms such as Core Banking System (CBS), National Cooperative Database (NCD), Common Service Centres (CSC) and other digital service platforms, enabling PACS to function as vibrant multipurpose economic institutions and provide diversified services to their members.
  10. Strengthening Governance Framework: The Ministry has undertaken several policy and institutional reforms, including establishment of the National Cooperative Database, formulation of the National Cooperation Policy, 2025, promotion of transparent and professionally managed cooperatives, and technology-driven monitoring systems to improve governance, accountability and ease of doing business in the cooperative sector.
  11. Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) have been allowed to open new branches to expand their business: UCBs can now open new branches up to 15% (maximum 10 branches) of the existing number of branches in the previous financial year without prior approval of the RBI.
  12. UCBs have been allowed by the RBI to offer doorstep services to their customers: Doorstep banking facility can now be provided by UCBs. Account holders of these banks can now avail various banking facilities at home, such as cash withdrawal, cash deposit, KYC, demand draft, and life certificate for pensioners, etc.
  13. Umbrella Organization for Urban Cooperative Banks: National Urban Cooperative Finance and Development Corporation (NUCFDC) has been established with the approval of the RBI as an Umbrella Organization (UO) for the UCB sector, which is providing necessary IT infrastructure and operational support to around 1,500 UCBs. It has launched various services like Digi Loan and Digi Pay.
  14. Cooperative banks have been allowed to make one-time settlement of outstanding loans, like Commercial Banks:  Co-operative banks, through board-approved policies, can now provide the process for settlement with borrowers, along with technical write-off.
  15. License fee reduced for Cooperative Banks for AePS: License fee for onboarding Cooperative Banks to ‘Aadhaar Enabled Payment System’ (AePS) has been reduced by linking it to the number of transactions. Cooperative financial institutions are now to get the facility free of cost for the first three months of the pre-production phase. With this, members of onboarded Banks are now able to get the facility of banking at their home through biometrics.
  16. UIDAI on 01.08.2025 has introduced a new framework for onboarding of Cooperative Banks on the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS). Now, only StCBs are required to onboard as Authentication User Agencies (AUA)/eKYC User Agencies (KUA); DCCBs will be allowed to use it through State Cooperative Bank as sub AUA/KUA, free of cost.
  17. Sahakar Sarathi (Shared Service Entity): Sahakar Sarathi (Shared Service Entity) Private Limited has been established after approval of the RBI to provide technological services to Rural Cooperative Banks (RCBs) and their strengthening. This has launched 13 services for the Rural Cooperative Banking Sector.
  18. RBI vide its Notification dated 07.10.2025, has included rural cooperative banks in its Integrated Ombudsman Scheme. This will bring more transparency and accountability to the functions of rural cooperative banks.
  19. RBI vide Master Direction dated 04.12 2025, has allowed State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) to open new branches (maximum 10) through an automatic route. StCBs & DCCBs, subject to eligibility, will now be able to open new branches without delay and can expand their business.
  20. RBI vide Master Direction dated 28.11.2025, has granted relaxation to the Rural and Urban cooperative banks in financial norms for providing modern banking services.  The previous requirements of Gross NPA being less than 7% and Net NPA not exceeding 3%, and the net profit criterion have been removed. Now the cooperative banks can easily provide modern banking services to their customers.
  21. RBI vide Master Direction dated 04.12.2025, has issued Eligibility Criteria norms for Business Authorisation (ECBA), which will supersede the previous FSWM provisions. The clause regarding no penalties in the last two years has been removed from these norms. Now the Cooperative Banks will be able to easily open new branches and expand their business.
  22. Promotion of Good Governance
  1. Cooperative Governance Index (CGI) for RCBs

A first-of-its-kind framework developed by NABARD to assess, quantify and benchmark governance standards in StCBs and DCCBs, supported by a digital portal with dashboards and role-based access.

Outcome: The CGI portal for RCBs went live on 01 April 2026, converting governance from a qualitative to a measurable, comparable and monitorable parameter and enabling targeted remedial action.

  1. Enhanced CAMELSC Framework, SuperSoft and risk-based supervision

NABARD introduced the Enhanced CAMELSC Framework in a graded manner in RCBs — an intermediate step towards Risk-Based Supervision — capturing governance, internal controls, IT risk and cyber-security parameters, supported by the digital supervisory platform SuperSoft for inspection, compliance tracking and supervisory analytics.

Outcome: A more data-driven, forward-looking and risk-sensitive supervisory ecosystem for the cooperative sector.

  1. Model policies aligned with RBI Master Directions

NABARD has initiated development of 26 model policies covering governance, IT, cyber security, audit, compliance and risk management, aligned with RBI's consolidated Master Directions, for uniform adoption by RCBs.

  1. Governance, capacity building and supervisory oversight

Institution-specific Turn Around Plans (TAPs) for weak banks, professionalisation of management, strengthening of internal audit and Board-level Audit/Risk Committees, and structured training of Directors, CEOs, credit, recovery and audit staff at NABARD's training establishments.

 

The reformative measures undertaken by the Ministry have significantly strengthened digital technology adoption, transparency and good governance in the cooperative sector. These initiatives have enabled digitization of cooperative institutions through ERP-based software, standardized accounting systems, digital record management, online monitoring, audit trails and real-time Management Information Systems (MIS), resulting in improved operational efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Overall, these digital interventions have promoted transparency, accountability, evidence-based decision-making and efficient governance, while facilitating better delivery of services to cooperative societies and their members across the country.

 

This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

COORDINATION BETWEEN NCOL AND STATE COOPERATIVE FEDERATIONS
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi

2298361.title: Safety Fencing Along 19,700 km of Railway Tracks to Prevent Trespassing and Ensure Safe Train Operations
2298361.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Safety Fencing Along 19,700 km of Railway Tracks to Prevent Trespassing and Ensure Safe Train Operations
Indian Railways Takes Legal Action Against Offenders of Stone Pelting Under Relevant Provisions of Law to Provide Safety to Passengers and Protect Railway Property
Awareness Programmes Including OPERATION SATHI to Sensitize People and Regular Coordination with GRP/Local Police to Curb Stone Pelting Incidents on Trains
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi

Legal action is taken against the offenders of stone pelting under the relevant provision of law. The following preventive measures are taken by the Railways to safeguard the lives of passengers and damage to Railway Property:

  • Regular drives are conducted against anti-social elements like drunkard, mischievous elements etc. in the effected section/black spots and the apprehended persons are prosecuted under legal provisions of law.
  • The train escorting parties have been sensitized to remain more vigilant in the vulnerable sections/spots, where incidents of vandalizing on trains are frequently reported.
  • Various awareness programme including OPERATION SATHI are conducted regularly in inhabited areas adjacent to Railway track to sensitize people towards the menace of stone pelting and its consequences.
  • Detailed guidelines have been issued regarding action to be taken to control incidents of stone pelting on moving trains. Analysis of these incidents followed by substantive action is taken to curb these incidents.
  • Regular co-ordination with GRP/Local Police is maintained by RPF, sharing the critical information to control the menace of pelting of stones on trains.
  • State Level Security Committee of Railways (SLSCR) have been constituted for all State Union Territories under the Chairmanship of respective Director General of Police Commissioner of States/Union Territories for regular monitoring and review of security arrangements of the Railways.

Safety of train operations is accorded top priority on Indian Railways (IR). Pedestrian subways are also being provided with safety fencing in order to facilitate crossing of railway alignment by cattle, pedestrians and smaller vehicles.

Till date, about 19,700 km of fencing has been provided along the railway tracks in Indian Railways which includes sections situated in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

This information was provided by the Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, in a reply to a question in the Lok Sabha today.

2298355.title: RailOne App Reaches 4.76 Crore Downloads, Records 10 Lakh Daily Average Ticket Bookings
2298355.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
RailOne App Reaches 4.76 Crore Downloads, Records 10 Lakh Daily Average Ticket Bookings
RailOne App Integrates Reserved, Unreserved & Platform Ticketing, Train & PNR Enquiry, RailMadad and Other Key Railway Services on a Single Platform
NTES Handles Over 6 Crore Daily Enquiries and 80,000 Concurrent Users, Reducing Queues & Waiting Time at Railway Enquiry Counters
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi

With a view to expand digital mode of procurement of reserved as well as unreserved tickets Railways has launched RailOne App on 01.07.2025. This App enables passengers to book reserved as well as unreserved tickets on mobile phone. This App combines all the public facing services of Indian Railways like reserved ticketing, unreserved ticketing and platform ticketing, train enquiry, PNR enquiry, Railmadad, etc. into a single platform. This, in effect, brings the Passenger reservation system facility to passenger's palm.  The App facilitates users to access multiple services through Single-Sign-On (SSO) facility eliminating the necessity of downloading multiple Applications of Railways & remembering several passwords.

The details of transactions through Railone app as on 02.08.2026 are as under: -

Daily Average tickets

10 lakhs

Reserved tickets

2.79 lakhs

Unreserved tickets

7.24 lakhs

Downloads

4.76 crores

 

The National Train Enquiry System (NTES), implemented in the year 2000, provides passengers with near real-time train running information, including arrival/departure status and train schedules through multiple interfaces such as enquiry counters, the NTES website, mobile applications (Android & iOS) and the nationwide Rail Enquiry Number 139. Its key features include Spot Your Train, Live Station, Train Schedule, and Trains between Stations, enabling passengers to access authentic and reliable information conveniently. The NTES mobile application, launched in October 2014 (Android) and October 2015 (iOS), has recorded more than 4.5 crore downloads on Android and 16 lakh downloads on iOS as on 01.08.2026. At present, NTES handles about 80,000 concurrent users and processes over 6 crore enquiries daily. It has been generally appreciated by the passengers.

The deployment of the National Train Enquiry System (NTES), which provides passengers with easy access to authentic and near real-time train running information through multiple digital platforms including the website, mobile applications and Rail Enquiry Number 139, has significantly reduced the need for passengers to visit railway enquiry counters. Consequently, this has helped in reducing queues and waiting time at enquiry counters.

In cases of train cancellation, the online e-ticketing system NGeT(Next Generation E-ticketing) automatically initiates the process of refund immediately after the scheduled time of departure of the train and the applicable refund is credited to the passenger's bank account. Automatic refunds linked to train cancellation are presently available only for e-Tickets booked online and are not available for counter tickets in which case the passenger holding counter ticket is required to visit nearest PRS counter.

RailOne is the Official App of Indian Railways which provides integrated platform for all public facing services of IR. It offers reserved, unreserved and platform ticketing, journey plan, train information, passenger support and allied railway services through a single, seamless mobile application.

Presently approximately 89% of the reserved tickets are booked online as compared to about 49% in 2013-14. Unreserved tickets booked through various non-counter modes has increased to nearly 39%.

This information was provided by the Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, in a reply to a question in the Lok Sabha today.

2298357.title: Central Government Strengthens Access to Higher Education for SC Students through POST-MATRIC SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME
2298357.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Central Government Strengthens Access to Higher Education for SC Students through POST-MATRIC SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME
Scheme Aims to INCREASE GROSS ENROLLMENT RATIO OF SC STUDENTS in Higher Education with Focus on Students from Poorest Households
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government is implementing the Post-Matric Scholarship (PMS) Scheme for Scheduled Caste (SC) students with the objective of appreciably increasing the GROSS ENROLLMENT RATIO OF SC students in higher education, with a focus on students from the poorest households. The scheme provides financial assistance at the post-matriculation or post-secondary stage to enable eligible students to complete their education.

In a written reply to Shri Brij Lal, Smt. Laxmi Verma and Shri Ryaga Krishnaiah in the Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale stated that the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme is open-ended and demand-driven for eligible students studying in all recognized institutions across the country.

He stated that Annual Action Plans under the scheme are obtained from States and Union Territories, which are the implementing agencies. The release of the Central share is contingent upon States and UTs transmitting their State/UT share-paid, finally verified data on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) for disbursement of the Central share.

Under the scheme, the scholarship is paid to students whose parents or guardians have an annual income from all sources not exceeding ₹2.5 lakh. The income eligibility criterion ensures that financial assistance is targeted towards eligible students requiring support to pursue and complete their post-matric and higher education.

The Government also provided details of Central Assistance released to Chhattisgarh under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students during the last five financial years. In 2021-22, ₹29.00 crore was released, benefiting 87,464 students. In 2022-23, ₹45.00 crore was released, benefiting 96,267 students. During 2023-24, ₹36.14 crore was released for 79,237 beneficiaries, while ₹39.96 crore was released in 2024-25, benefiting 87,675 students. In 2025-26, Central Assistance increased to ₹53.60 crore, benefiting 96,839 students.

During the five-year period from 2021-22 to 2025-26, a total Central Assistance of ₹203.70 crore was released to Chhattisgarh under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students, benefiting 4,47,482 students.

The Government's response highlights the demand-driven nature of the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme and its focus on enabling eligible SC students, particularly those from the poorest households, to pursue and complete higher education.

2298353.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Allocation Stands At ₹705.11 Crore In 2023-24, ₹539.44 Crore In 2024-25 And ₹557.42 Crore In 2025-26, Amounting To A Total Allocation Of ₹1,801.97 Crores Over The Three-Year Period Under WELFARE SCHEMES FOR SENIOR CITIZENS
No Pending Applications Under SHREYAS-SC; NO REDUCTION IN DE-ADDICTION CENTRE ALLOCATION DURING LAST THREE YEARS
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 4:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has clarified the status of scholarship applications and unpaid scholarship dues for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Persons with Disabilities (PwDs), while also providing details of budget allocations for de-addiction centres and welfare schemes for senior citizens.

In a written reply to Dr. Menaka Guruswamy in the Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale stated that the Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes & Others and the Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students are Centrally Sponsored Schemes that are open-ended and demand-driven.

He stated that the scholarships are released through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries adding that the release of the Central share is contingent upon the concerned State Government or UT Administration releasing its share and uploading the finally verified paid data on the National Scholarship Portal.

Under the Central Sector Scheme of Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme for SCs (SHREYAS-SC), the Government stated that no scholarship application is pending and there are no unpaid scholarship dues.

On allocations for de-addiction centres, the Government clarified that there has been no reduction in budget allocation during the last three years.

For welfare schemes for senior citizens, the allocation stood at ₹705.11 crore in 2023-24, ₹539.44 crore in 2024-25 and ₹557.42 crore in 2025-26, amounting to a total allocation of ₹1,801.97 crores over the three-year period.

 

 

The Government further informed that the Prime Minister Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India for OBCs and others (PM-YASASVI) comprises four sub-schemes—Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top-Class Education in Colleges and Top-Class Education in Schools for OBC, EBC and DNT students.

The Pre-Matric and Post-Matric components are Centrally Sponsored Schemes, with processing, verification, sanction and disbursement undertaken by the respective State Governments and UT Administrations, while the Central Government releases funds to the States and UTs. The Top-Class Education in Schools and Top-Class Education in Colleges components are Central Sector Schemes.

With regard to students with disabilities, the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) is implementing the Central Sector “Scholarship Scheme for Students with Disabilities”. Applications received under the scheme are processed in accordance with the prevailing scheme guidelines, subject to fulfilment of prescribed eligibility conditions and submission of complete applications. Sanction and release of scholarships are undertaken continuously during the academic year.

The Government's response highlights the demand-driven nature of key scholarship schemes, the DBT-based mechanism for scholarship disbursement, and the continuous processing of eligible applications under the respective schemes.

2298342.title: Parliament Question: Vacancies in Universities
2298342.body_html:
Ministry of Education
Parliament Question: Vacancies in Universities
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi

Education being a subject of the Concurrent List of the Constitution, both the Centre and States/ UTs are responsible for the Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and Schools in the country. 

The Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs) under the Ministry of Education including Central Universities, are statutory autonomous organizations established under respective Central Acts of Parliament and governed by provisions of the  Acts/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations made thereunder. As autonomous institutions, faculty recruitment is done within the institutions itself, in accordance with their Acts and Regulations. The recruitment powers vests with the respective Board of Governors/Executive  Committee/Board of Management.

State Universities are established through respective State Acts and vacancies therein are filled by concerned State Governments/ Universities themselves. Vacancy details of State Universities are not maintained centrally. 

An Institution is declared as Deemed to be University by the Central Government, on the advice of University Grants Commission (UGC), under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. The  Institutions Deemed to be Universities are regulated by the UGC as per the UGC (Institutions  deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2023. As per these Regulations, the Executive Council of the Institution appoints faculty staff and such other posts on the recommendation of the Selection Committee, in accordance with the University Grants Commission (Minimum  Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and other Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges and other Measures for the Maintenance of Standards in Higher Education)  Regulations, 2018.

Occurring of vacancies and filling thereof is a continuous process. The vacancies arise due to  promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening of new institutions, schemes or projects, and additional requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength and expansion of capacity  in existing institutions. 

In centrally financed Higher Education Institutions, measures have been taken to attract quality faculties which includes year-round open advertisements, recruitment through search-cum selection procedures, special recruitment drive, mission mode recruitment and invitation to  alumni/scientists/faculty, etc. The faculty recruitment processes are carried out by the CHEIs by inviting applications in a transparent manner, as part of a multi-step and robust screening process. The Acts and Statutes of various institutions specify the composition of selection  committees, authorities responsible for recruitment of various levels of faculty, provision of  independent subject experts and visitor’s nominees etc. so as to ensure transparency and academic rigour in recruitments. UGC has launched a common portal ‘CU-CHAYAN’ for  faculty recruitment, making provision for listing of vacancies/ advertisements/ jobs across all Central Universities, thus making the entire recruitment process more transparent and accessible. 

The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, lays emphasis on improving the overall quality of education in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) through a set of initiatives that include promotion of multidisciplinary education, nurturing critical thinking and analytical ability, promoting research and innovation, improving the quality of infrastructure, effective and qualitative teacher training etc. 

To improve the quality of education, several initiatives have been institutionalised in centrally funded institutions. The Government of India provides financial support to state governments under Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA)/ Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM USHA) scheme, for improvement in Higher Education. The Government of India has also launched the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Program (MMTTP) in 2023 across the country to improve teaching quality, strengthen institutional performance, and promote better academic outcomes in Higher Educational Institutions. The program is implemented through 151 Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centres (MMTTCs). So far, more than 4 lakh faculty members have been trained across the country. 

In August, 2021, all CHEIs under the Ministry of Education were requested to undertake a special drive to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook  special recruitment drives to fill the vacancies including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled  Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In September 2022, the Ministry of Education had also exhorted all the CHEIs to fill up the vacancies in Mission Mode. In October 2025, all the CHEIs have again been requested to fill up all the backlog vacancies in Mission Mode.  From September 2022, all CHEIs including Central Universities (CUs) have undertaken Mission Mode recruitment drives to fill the vacancies. Up to 23.05.2026 (i.e. the date of the last  Rozgar Mela), a total number of 32,114 posts have been filled up by all CHEIs, including 18,757  faculty positions, in Mission Mode.  

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2298340.title: PREPARATORY ACTIVITIES FOR CENSUS 2027
2298340.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
PREPARATORY ACTIVITIES FOR CENSUS 2027
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 4:52PM by PIB Delhi

First phase of the Census 2027 i.e., Houselisting and Housing Census has already been completed in 31 States/UTs. In the remaining states first phase of the census is scheduled to be completed by September, 2026. Further, as per the notification dated 3rd August, 2026 in the Gazette of India, second phase of the Census i.e. Population Enumeration in the UT of Ladakh and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the UT of Jammu & Kashmir and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the States of Himachal Pradesh and Uttrakhand shall be undertaken from 1st September, 2026 to 30th September, 2026 with a revisional round from 1st  October, 2026 to 5th  October, 2026. There shall also be an option for self-enumeration from 17thAugust, 2026 to 31st August, 2026.

Mobile applications for data collection and other digital platforms, including the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) Portal, have been deployed for the conduct of the first phase of Census 2027. The facility of self-enumeration to the respondents through an online web portal has also been given for the first time in Census. Digital tools for the second phase of the census have been developed. 

Training of Master Trainers, Field Trainers, Enumerators, Supervisors etc. for the first phase of Census 2027 has been completed/ in progress, in accordance with the notified schedule, in coordination with the States/ UTs Government.

Till now, a total amount of ₹4102 crore have already been released to States/UTs for training of Census functionaries, manpower assistance, technical infrastructure, payment of honorarium to Census functionaries etc.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha

2298339.title: Parliament Question: Regulations of Education Fees
2298339.body_html:
Ministry of Education
Parliament Question: Regulations of Education Fees
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi

Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution. Schools, other than those established, owned or controlled by the Central Government, are under the jurisdiction of the respective State Governments/UT Administrations. Therefore, matters related to the management of schools that are not established, owned or controlled by the Central Government are regulated in accordance with the rules and instructions of the respective State Government/UT administrations.

In view of the above, matters relating to fees charged by private schools, the rules/regulations for safeguarding the interests of students and their parents; and action against violating schools comes under the jurisdiction of the respective state governments/UT administrations. However, under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, every child aged six to fourteen has the right to free and compulsory elementary education in a neighborhood school. Section 12(1) (c) of the RTE Act, 2009 mandates reservation in private unaided schools for children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups to the extent of at least 25% seats at the entry level and provision of free and compulsory elementary education to such children till its completion. Also, Section 13 of the RTE Act, 2009 clearly prohibits the collection of any capitation fee.

Institutions deemed to be Universities are regulated by UGC (Institutions deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2023. Regulation 24.B.(2) mandates that these institutions follow rules on fee structure and seat numbers set by relevant statutory bodies. As far as private colleges/universities are concerned, private universities are established by an Act of the concerned state legislature and are governed by the provisions of their respective Act and norms/rules/regulations made by the respective state govt., for the purpose including fee related matters. 

The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has established bye-laws that regulate various aspects of school administration, including fee structures for private schools affiliated with the Board. The bye-laws require express approval from the School Management Committee or adherence to the process prescribed by the appropriate government for any fee revision. Also, the CBSE has taken steps to prevent schools from exploiting parents through mandatory purchases. CBSE guidelines prohibit schools from compelling students to buy books, uniforms, or stationery from specific vendors. This aims to reduce the financial burden on parents and promote fair competition.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

*****

2298338.title: DRUG TRAFFICKING CASES
2298338.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
DRUG TRAFFICKING CASES
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has adopted a multi-pronged approach to curb cross-border smuggling including drugs, some of which are as under: -

 

(i)       Deployment of advanced surveillance equipment such as CCTV, drones, automatic number plate recognition systems, Pan, Tilt & Zoom (PTZ) Camera, Night Vision Device (NVD).

(ii)      Development of fencing, border outposts, roads, and helipads to enhance vigilance and mobility of security forces.

(iii)     Intensified area domination through patrolling, Naka points, and mobile teams to monitor illegal activities.

(iv)     Close collaboration between intelligence agencies and other organizations for real-time information sharing through established platforms.

(v)      Identification and management of designated entry/exit points to ensure controlled movement of people and goods.

 

Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) was launched on 15th August 2020 by Department of Social Justice & Empowerment in 272 identified most vulnerable Districts. It has been extended to all districts of the country since August 2023. Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan intends to reach out to the masses and spread awareness about substance use with focus on higher educational Institutions, university campuses & schools. With the constant support of all the States, NMBA has been able to reach and sensitize more than 29.05 Crore people, including more than 11.05 Crore youth and 7.81 Crore women, through extensive awareness and outreach activities conducted across the country. 1.17 lakh + Nasha Mukti Mitr have joined the campaign.

To strengthen Centre-State framework to dismantle drug-trafficking networks Government has taken various measures, some of which are as under: -

(i)     To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) has been released on 26.06.2026. The Vision Document is to be implemented by the concerned Central Ministries/ Departments/ Agencies and the State Governments/UTs as per the action points and timelines specifically mentioned for each Central Ministry/ Department/ Agency. The four key focus areas outlined in the vision document are as under: -

 

  1. Enforcement (Intelligence & Operations)
  2. Precursors & Synthetic Drugs Control
  3. Demand & Harm Reduction
  4. Capacity Building & Coordination

 

(ii)    Established a 4-tier (Apex and Executive Committee at Central level and State and District level Committee at the State level) Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism for ensuring better coordination between Central & State Drug Law Enforcement Agencies and other stakeholders in the field of controlling drug trafficking and drug abuse in India. State-level NCORD meetings are chaired by the Chief Secretary while District-level NCORD meetings are held under the chairmanship of the District Magistrate to review enforcement, intelligence sharing and preventive measures.

 

(iii)   The NCORD Portal, developed by Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), serves as a comprehensive gateway and Knowledge Management System for all stakeholders from district to central levels.

 

(iv)   Joint Coordination Committee (JCC) meetings are held regularly in which all relevant Central and State agencies participate, to discuss investigation of important narcotics cases in the State. So far 11 JCC meetings at Central level and 75 JCC at the State level have been conducted.

 

(v)    A dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) headed by Additional Director General/ Inspector General level Police Officer is established in each State/UT to function as the NCORD Secretariat for the State/UT and follow-up on compliance of decisions taken in NCORD meetings at different levels.

 

 (vi)  NCB, has shared a list of habitual narcotics offenders operating across the country with the State Police. The list was circulated to facilitate identification and initiation of suitable preventive action, including consideration of detention under the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PITNDPS) Act, 1988, against repeat and high-risk drug traffickers. The Drug Law Enforcement Agency (DLEAs) have effectively utilized the provisions of the PITNDPS Act and invoked detention orders against 810 habitual drug offenders all over the county during 2025 and 427 till June, 2026.

2298337.title: Parliament Question: Availability of Special Educators in Schools
2298337.body_html:
Ministry of Education
Parliament Question: Availability of Special Educators in Schools
Posted On: 12 AUG 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi

Education is a subject under the Concurrent List of the Constitution and the majority of schools are under the administrative control of the respective state governments and Union Territory (UT) administrations. The Department of School Education & Literacy is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha to support States and UTs in providing equitable and inclusive quality education from pre-primary to Class XII.

Under the Samagra Shiksha framework, recruitment and other service matters relating to teachers, including Special Educators, fall within the domain of the respective State Governments/UT Administrations. The framework also provides for Special Educators to be deployed at the block or cluster level, as per requirement, and to work in an itinerant mode, covering a group of schools where Children with Special Needs (CwSN) are enrolled, so that their educational needs are adequately addressed.

Under Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI (PM Schools for Rising India), financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for strengthening school education, including maintaining appropriate Pupil-Teacher Ratios (PTRs) and supporting inclusive education. This includes provision for two Resource Persons for CwSN at each Block Resource Centre (BRC).

The Department has notified the Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) for Special Educators in general schools for CwSN vide Notification No. S.O. 4586(E) dated 21.09.2022, published on 29.09.2022, as follows:

(i)  One Special Educator for every 10 CwSN at the primary level; and

(ii) One Special Educator for every 15 CwSN at the upper-primary level.

 

As per UDISE+ 2025–26, 1.17 lakh schools have a dedicated Special Educator. A statement indicating the State/UT-wise details of enrolment of CwSN and the number of schools having a dedicated Special Educator, as per UDISE+ 2025–26, is placed at Annexure.

The Department also supports capacity building of teachers and special educators through continuous professional development, in-service training, and awareness and sensitization programmes on inclusive education. National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has developed online teacher training modules under National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement (NISHTHA) for the Elementary, Secondary and Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) stages, equipping general teachers to address the diverse learning needs of CwSN. NCERT and Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) have also developed handbooks on Inclusive Education to provide practical guidance to teachers for addressing the diverse needs of children in inclusive classrooms.

Further, the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) has integrated two dedicated credits on Inclusive Education for CwSN in the Four-Year Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP) for pre-service teacher education. This is aimed at equipping prospective teachers with the knowledge and skills required to ensure inclusion and meaningful participation of CwSN in regular schools and to adapt teaching-learning processes to address diverse learning needs, including those associated with learning disabilities.

The Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI), a statutory body of the Government of India responsible for regulating and monitoring the training of rehabilitation professionals and personnel, is mandated to develop human resources in 16 categories of rehabilitation professionals/personnel. RCI has granted approval to 1,081 institutions/universities to offer courses in disability rehabilitation and special education, thereby contributing to the availability of qualified human resources, including Special Educators.
